items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: Rae sang, 'Precious Lord,' a gospel hymn written by Tommy Dorsey.

ctx.x: The Mt. Morris Presbyterian Church resounded with music as the Sam Wooding-Rae Harrison Jazz Band poured on the jazz at a memorial benefit concert, Sunday, Oct. 19.

The concert billed as, 'Sweet and Sacred Jazz,' featured Sam Wooding and Rae Harrison along with their eleven man band. Sam Wooding, an energetic 85, wrote most of the jazz selections and conducted the entire program. His vivacious partner and wife, Rae Harrison performed the spiritual and blues songs. For starters, Rae sang, 'Precious Lord,' a gospel hymn written by Tommy Dorsey. Singing slowly, her rich voice resonated throughout the vaulted and glass-domed sanctuary. Rae nursed the words and concluded by…

Introducing the next number, Sam said, 'Our people brought old melodies from Africa, called the blues. This next number, 'Kater Street Blues,' tells about the mean and ugly street I grew up in Philadelphia.'
